constraints.note: Try to leave 10 hours between a close and the next day's open.
Nobody works more than 5 days a week.
A manager on duty whenever we're open.
Spread closes: at most 3 per person.
Yael and Lane shouldn't work together.

narrative:
We're open 11am to 10pm Monday through Thursday, till 11pm Friday and Saturday, and 9pm on Sunday. Prep starts two hours before we open. The owner gives me 804 hours a week for the whole crew. No overtime. There's always a manager on the floor when the doors are open. Doubles are normal here: people work lunch, go home, and come back for dinner. Nobody comes in for less than 3 hours. Thursday we've got a private party, a rehearsal dinner for about 40, 6pm to 10pm, so I need two extra servers, a second bartender and another cook on the line. Lunch is 11 to 2, dinner rush 5 to 9, and Friday and Saturday nights are way busier. Keep Yael and Lane off the same shift, trust me. The high school kids can't come in before 3 on weekdays.

We're in Chicago, so the schedule has to go up 14 days ahead, and changing it after it's posted costs us premium pay. Corporate posts it on time. A clopen with less than 10 hours between shifts gets paid at 1.25x for those hours here, so I'd rather not. Anyone on past 7.5 hours gets a 20-minute meal break, leaders too. Chicago minimum wage is $17.05; nobody here makes less than that. Blake is 15, mostly on server, and has been helping out on the fryer when we're slammed.
